cards.explanation: The answer is a house for the ark of the covenant. David says it was in his heart to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and as a footstool for our God. He wasn't just daydreaming with his feet up, friends. He tells the crowd he'd already gotten ready to build it.

The answer is True. David says, “I had made preparations to build it…” so the plans were already moving. This king didn't just say 'someday.' He had his apron on and the oven warm. I think that makes the next part even harder to hear.

The answer is that David is a man of war who has shed blood. David tells the crowd God said, “You are not to build a house for My Name, because you are a man of war who has shed blood.” That's a heavy thing to say out loud in front of everybody. I think it took real humility for David to repeat it to the whole room.

The answer is Judah. David says, “…He chose Judah as leader…” and then he zooms in. From the house of Judah God chose his father's household, and from his father's sons God was pleased to make him king over all Israel. It's like a map app, friends: tribe, then household, then one king in the middle of it all.

The answer is Solomon. Solomon, David's son, is the one David says the LORD has chosen to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel. David says the LORD has given him many sons, and still the choice is one. Many sons, one throne.

The answers are son and Father. God says of Solomon, “…for I have chosen him as My son, and I will be his Father.” That's not a small word to hear from God, friends. David is repeating it right there in front of the whole room, passing along the words just as he heard them.

The condition is that Solomon resolutely carries out God's commandments. God says, “I will establish his kingdom forever, if he resolutely carries out My commandments and ordinances…” The word is resolutely, friends. That means no halfway and no 'I'll get to it Thursday.'

The answer is that they possess the good land and pass it down. David says to keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, “…so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your descendants forever.” So the purpose he gives covers the land now and an inheritance for descendants later. He says it in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD.

The answer is that the LORD searches every heart. David tells Solomon to serve with a willing mind “…for the LORD searches every heart and understands the intent of every thought.” That's a lot of searching, friends. You can't hand God a cookie that only looks good on top.

The answer is True. David tells Solomon, “If you seek Him, He will be found by you…” He says it right after telling Solomon to know the God of his father and serve Him wholeheartedly. That's David's word to his son.

The answer is False. David tells Solomon, “…if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever.” It sits right next to the promise that seeking Him means finding Him. It's a heavy line, so I think David wanted Solomon to hear it plainly.

The answer is that the LORD made the details clear to David in writing. David says, “…the LORD has made clear to me in writing by His hand upon me.” So the plan didn't come from David's own sketch pad. Every detail was made clear to him by the LORD.

The answer is True. David tells Solomon, “Do not be afraid or discouraged, for the LORD God, my God, is with you.” Notice that David says my God. He's handing his son the job of building the house, and he's telling him the LORD God is with him.

The word is house. David says the LORD will neither fail nor forsake Solomon “…before all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.” So the promise lasts all the way to the last bit of work. That's the stretch David names, friends.

The answer is every willing man of every skill. David says, “…every willing man of every skill will be at your disposal for the work.” Willing and skilled, friends. That's the kind of crew you want in any kitchen.
